points.description: States that the best-case number of operations is N (equivalently linear/O(N) time), where N is the length of the array.
States that the best-case scenario is an input array that is already sorted (in non-decreasing order).

rubric.notes: Full marks require both the best-case operation count (N/linear, with N the array length) and the best-case input (an already sorted array). Award the relevant point(s) for each correct part. No marks for claiming the best case is quadratic or that a reverse-sorted array is the best case.
